To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

sulfidogenic biotreatment of wastewaters containing high concentrations of organic matter and sulfate can be achieved in continuous packed-bed bioreactors with ferrous chloride dosing, and that recycling of the sludge materials collected from the bioreactors can improve treatment performance.

sulfidogenic biotreatment with ferrous chloride addition and sludge recycling can be used to treat wastewater with a wide range of COD/sodium sulfate ratios, with a COD/sulfate ratio of 2 being optimal for high COD removal and low iron release.

sulfidogenic biotrickling filter (BTF) with ferrous chloride dosing can achieve stable continuous wastewater treatment over 450-day period with 84 ±9% COD removal and 94 ±6% sulfate reduction under optimal chemical loading and sludge recycling conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel continuous sulfidogenic wastewater biotreatment process with iron sulfide oxidation and recycle, and it is expected that this process can be used for treating sulfidic wastewaters containing organic carbon, such as acid mine drainage, and other sulfidic wastestreams with organic carbon, such sulfate-rich industrial wastewaters.
the technical feasibility of the sulfidogenic biotreatment of wastewater with iron sulfide (FeS) sludge oxidation and recycling.
a novel sulfidogenic wastewater process with iron sulfide (FeS) sludge recycling and oxidation for the first time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sulfidogenic biotreatment with iron sulfide recycling can be a promising approach for continuous wastewater treatment.
the sulfidogenic packed-bed reactors with sludge recycling can be a promising technology for the treatment of sulfate-rich wastewater.
sulfidogenic packed bed bioreactors can be used for continuous wastewater treatment with the ability to recycle iron sulfide slurry to improve treatment performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this sulfidogenic process with iron sulfide oxidation and recycle is technically feasible, and could be a promising technology for treating wastewater containing high concentrations of COD and sulfate.
the bioreactors are able to absorb changes in the influent chemical load, and the recycling of the sludge materials is a viable strategy to improve the treatment performance.
the packed-bed sulfidogen bioreactors are capable of treating high strength wastewater under a wide range of chemical load combinations with or without recycling of iron sulfide sludges.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sulfidogenic bioprocess can be effectively stabilized by the recycling of the sludge materials, which can help reduce the sludge disposal costs and improve treatment performance.
the sulfidogenic biotrickling filter system with sludge recycle is technically feasible for treating wastewater under a COD/sulfate ratio of 2 with an Fe/S molar loading ratio of 1.
sulfidogenic biotechnology has great potential in treating wastewater streams with high sulfate concentrations, and the process can be improved with sludge oxidation and recycling.
